chapter: Rhythm and blues, the Howard Theatre and later years
title: Tiny Bradshaw's band in 1953
summary: Phillips played with Bradshaw in Washington, Baltimore and the Apollo; Bradshaw sang sentimental songs, wrote Soft and Jersey Bounce and was a showman front man.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then you played with Tiny Bradshaw in '53.
Was that around town, or was that on the road?
Here and Baltimore and at the Apollo.
What kind of band did he have?
Same. About six pieces. We was just the addition.
No, Tiny played most everything in his pband. He had a lot of tunes he saw. He'd sing "After You've
Gone" and sentimental tunes like that, and he had a tune called "Soft" -- that was his tune. What's this other tune that he wrote? "Jersey Bounce."
Did he ever play with Hines?

Lucky Millinder. He played with the (?) band. He didn't play nothin' with his band. He'd just stand in front of the thing. He was a front man, a helluva front man in front of a band. Dance and do all them different things, you know.
